hook: Yes, it runs on all five machines
items: Flagship phone: Yes, Pac-Man model, int8, about 460 KB, estimated
Laptop, 8 GB, no GPU: Yes, Pac-Man model, int8, about 460 KB, estimated
MacBook Air, 16 GB: Yes, Pac-Man model, int8, about 460 KB, estimated
RTX 4060, 8 GB: Yes, Pac-Man model, int8, about 460 KB, estimated
RTX 4090, 24 GB: Yes, Pac-Man model, int8, about 460 KB, estimated
Breakout 99.99: Author reports 99.99 of 100 next frames predicted exactly right
Doom-lite 60 to 84: A second pass lifts exact frames from 60 to 84 of 100
Pac-Man 86.4: Author reports 86 of 100 next frames predicted exactly right
the_catch: Scores skip frames right after a random event. Doom-lite's number looks worse than it plays. Frame rate on the Pico itself is not measured yet.

caption: A world model small enough for a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W board. The author says the largest game, Pac-Man, needs about 460 KB of RAM on the board, so any phone or laptop has room. The scores come from the author's own README. Save this sheet for the next tiny model. Which would you run first: Pong or Pac-Man?
alt_text: A cheat sheet for the tinyworldformer world model. Five machines from a flagship phone to an RTX 4090 are each marked Yes, followed by three benchmark lines about how many next frames the model predicts exactly right.
